manifest_row.title: Rivers ensure one-third of carbon from fires is stored in the ocean

screening.main_topic: Research on how rivers transport fire-derived black carbon to the oceans, where it can be stored for long periods.
screening.climate_relevance: The article links wildfire-derived carbon storage to the carbon cycle and explains that climate change may increase wildfire frequency, intensity, and size, potentially strengthening this long-term carbon-storage feedback.
screening.reason: Although the study focuses on river transport and ocean storage of black carbon, its findings are explicitly connected to climate change, wildfire projections, and a climate feedback loop.
